top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: A 50 per cent US tariff on nearly US$20 billion of Canadian goods took effect on Saturday after trade talks collapsed minutes before the deadline, and Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will hit back dollar for dollar. The war news was grim in both directions: the death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre settled at 16, while Russian officials said Ukrainian drones killed at least six people overnight inside Russia. Washington and Tehran spent the day trading defiant statements ahead of Monday's sanctions package, even as Iran quietly waved a handful of Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Elsewhere the pattern was violence against soft targets, most starkly a Myanmar air strike that killed 14 people sheltering at a Buddhist monastery. Monday is the day to watch — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has promised 'the toughest sanctions in history'.

stories.headline: US hits Canadian goods with 50% tariffs after trade talks collapse
stories.summary: A fresh wave of US tariffs on Canadian goods took effect on Saturday after negotiations broke down minutes before the Friday-night deadline. President Donald Trump had threatened a 50 per cent levy on nearly US$20 billion (C$28 billion) of Canadian imports by Aug 19 before pausing it earlier in the week. Prime Minister Mark Carney said he suspended talks because “last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic”, and that Canada would retaliate “dollar for dollar”. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada had “declined to finalise the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week”.

stories.headline: Kryvyi Rih shopping centre death toll rises to 16 as rescuers dig through the night
stories.summary: Sixteen people were killed and 130 injured when two Russian drones hit a busy shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih in quick succession on Friday, in what Ukraine describes as a double-tap strike. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said the toll rose to 16 after another body was recovered overnight and that four people remain missing, with 52 injured — including 14 children — still in hospital. President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack, in his home city, “cynical and despicable”. Russia’s military has not commented.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit Ozon warehouse and Samara refinery; Russian officials report six dead
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones killed at least six civilians overnight in a wave of strikes on Russia, Russian regional officials said on Saturday. Samara Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said an industrial facility was hit; Ukraine’s military said it struck the region’s Novokuibyshevsk refinery, causing a fire. Ozon, Russia’s second-largest online retailer, said work at its Chapayevsk logistics centre had halted after a strike that caused injuries — the first on Ozon after weeks of attacks on rival Wildberries. Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said two children were killed at the Sea of Azov port town of Yeysk. The Russian accounts have not been independently verified.
stories.source: The Straits Times (Russian regional officials, Ukraine's military)

stories.headline: US and Iran trade defiant messages ahead of Monday’s sanctions package
stories.summary: With the war approaching six months, Washington and Tehran are neither exchanging fire nor holding talks. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will hold a press conference at 2pm EDT on Monday, having promised “the toughest sanctions in history” and urged China — which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran’s shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler — to cooperate. Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the coming measures an “assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations”. Beijing has urged diplomacy.

stories.headline: Iran lets a number of Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has granted permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported. Iraqi President Nizar Amedi said on Saturday that Iran had facilitated the passage of vessels carrying Iraqi oil in recent days, but called the issue complicated. Traffic through the strait remains far below pre-war levels and ships continue to face attacks. Iraq produced around 4 million barrels a day before the war and is working to expand exports through Turkey, Syria and Jordan.
stories.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Iraqi President Nizar Amedi)

stories.headline: Swedish police probe online networks after teenage girl killed in school sword attack
stories.summary: Swedish investigators are examining online communities that “might have egged on the suspect” after an 18-year-old man armed with a sword attacked the Brinell School in Fagersta, north-west of Stockholm, on Friday. A 17-year-old girl was killed and three others wounded, two of them seriously. Police said the suspect has been arrested and the case is being investigated as murder and attempted murder; media reported he was a former student at the school.

stories.headline: Myanmar military air strike on a Buddhist monastery kills 14, witnesses say
stories.summary: A fighter jet bombed a monastery compound in Swel Le Oh village in Myaung township, about 75km west of Mandalay, at around 9am on Friday, killing 11 men and three women and injuring about 20 more, according to a rebel fighter who saw the aftermath and local residents. More than 100 people were staying in and around the monastery for a weeklong Buddhist Lent retreat. A villager told AP the plane dropped two bombs 15 minutes apart. Myanmar’s military has not commented; the accounts come from opposition sources and witnesses and have not been independently verified.
stories.source: CNA, Al Jazeera, AP (via The Washington Post)

stories.headline: North Korea says a record-high Japanese defence budget would risk regional ‘turmoil’
stories.summary: Pyongyang has attacked Japan’s planned record defence spending, with state news agency KCNA saying the move — which is not yet finalised — “clearly signifies a dangerous expansion of the war budget that will bring new turmoil to the region and the world”. The statement lands as Washington scales back joint exercises with Seoul and President Donald Trump signals he wants another meeting with Kim Jong Un this year.

stories.headline: South Korean container ship sets sail to test an Arctic commercial route
stories.summary: A South Korean container ship has departed to trial a commercial Arctic shipping route, a priority for President Lee Jae Myung in a country that is one of the world’s shipping powerhouses. The voyage has drawn concern in the West because the Northern Sea Route runs along Russia’s coast, and comes as Hormuz disruption pushes shippers to look for alternatives.

stories.headline: TikTok to pay US$400 million to settle US children’s privacy case
stories.summary: TikTok and parent ByteDance have agreed to pay US$400 million to end a 2024 Department of Justice lawsuit alleging they collected “vast amounts of data” on millions of users under 13, in breach of the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act. Under the deal, US$300 million is paid immediately and US$100 million when the government vacates a 2019 FTC consent decree. Assistant Attorney-General Brett Shumate said “children and parents are better protected today than they were when this case began”. It is one of the largest COPPA settlements to date; YouTube paid US$170 million in 2019 and Epic Games US$275 million in 2022.

stories.headline: Imran Khan’s party files a contempt petition over the jailed ex-PM’s hospital move
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf has filed a contempt petition against the government after former prime minister Imran Khan was returned to prison from hospital. The petition also asks that Khan be treated at the private hospital specified by the court. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and says the cases against him are politically motivated; the government denies this.

stories.headline: Pentagon fires the top editor and publisher of Stars and Stripes
stories.summary: The Pentagon has dismissed the editor-in-chief and publisher of Stars and Stripes, the newspaper that has covered the US military since the Civil War, the publication’s leadership told US media on Aug 21. Editor-in-chief Erik Slavin told CBS News he was fired for “insubordination” after an interview in which he described disagreements with the Department of Defence, which said earlier in 2026 that it wanted to steer coverage away from “woke distractions”. Publisher Max Lederer, in post since 2007, was also terminated days after announcing his retirement; reporter Lara Korte said she was sacked too.

stories.headline: US judge strikes down the suspension of immigrant visas for 75 countries
stories.summary: US District Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan struck down a Trump administration policy suspending immigrant visa issuance to applicants from 75 countries, ruling on Aug 21 that it exceeded Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s statutory authority and was “patently unlawful”. The State Department policy, announced and in force since January, affected applicants from Latin American, Balkan and other nations.

stories.headline: Boeing engineers reject a contract offer and authorise a strike
stories.summary: The 17,000 members of SPEEA, the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, voted 64 per cent and 72 per cent against Boeing’s four-year offer and gave their negotiating team the power to call a strike when the contract expires on Oct 6, union officials said on Aug 21. Members cited wage increases capped at 3 per cent against Seattle inflation of 4.5 per cent. Boeing says it will implement a strike contingency plan.

stories.headline: Netherlands fines Uber €825 million over automated driver deactivations
stories.summary: The Dutch data protection authority confirmed on Aug 21 a €825 million (S$1.2 billion) fine against Uber for deactivating drivers’ accounts without telling them, a judgement agreed on Aug 17. The ruling rests on European data rules stating that people should not “be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing”. The case covers incidents between 2020 and 2022 and began with a complaint in France, but was heard in the Netherlands because Uber’s European headquarters are in Amsterdam. Uber says it contests the decision and the “disproportionate” fine.

stories.headline: Germany investigates possible Russian links to a weapons cache found in woods
stories.summary: German intelligence believes a cache of guns found in woodland near Berlin last year was intended for assassinations carried out on Russia’s behalf, according to reports. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said federal prosecutors are investigating a suspect in Romania over suspected espionage and “the preparation of a serious act of violence threatening the state”. Dobrindt declined to confirm the reported Russian link but said he could not rule out “the involvement of foreign powers”.

stories.headline: Two injured in a stabbing at a Sikh temple in Edmonton
stories.summary: A man has been arrested after two people were injured in an early-morning stabbing inside the Nanaksar Gurdwara in Edmonton, Canadian police said. The attack unfolded at about 5am local time on Friday; police have not identified the suspect or specified a motive. It follows threatening calls to two gurdwaras in Calgary that police confirmed they were investigating last week. The World Sikh Organization called the attack deeply troubling and pointed to rising anti-Sikh hate in Canada.

stories.headline: Tigray cancels its Ashenda festival over fears of drone strikes
stories.summary: The mass gathering at the centre of the Ashenda festival — a major religious and cultural celebration for women and the Virgin Mary — has been cancelled in Mekelle, the main city of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, over fears it could be targeted from the air. Tigray is still recovering from a two-year civil war that ended in 2022, and regional authorities blame recent deadly drone strikes on federal forces.

stories.headline: UK, Canada and Australia call Israel’s refusal to open an aid-worker probe ‘shameful’
stories.summary: The three governments issued a joint statement describing as “shameful” Israel’s decision not to open a criminal investigation into 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy in Gaza that killed seven humanitarian workers — three British nationals, a Pole, an Australian, a Canadian and a dual US-Canadian citizen. “The victims of this incident and their families deserve justice and accountability,” the foreign ministries said. Israel’s ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, defended the decision.

stories.headline: Turkey to seek an Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case
stories.summary: Turkey said on Aug 21 it would seek an Interpol red notice for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as part of a domestic criminal case linked to an attack on activists trying to deliver aid to Gaza, accusing Israel of genocide and crimes against humanity. Israel denies the charges and dismissed the move as a “pathetic attempt” to intimidate its leaders and soldiers; Netanyahu called President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an “antisemitic dictator”.

stories.headline: NATO’s top commander convenes allies on Hormuz — but ‘this is not a NATO mission’
stories.summary: Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, a spokesperson for NATO’s supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, said on Friday. “To be clear, this is not a NATO mission,” the spokesperson added. Allies have sought to avoid direct involvement in the Iran conflict.

stories.headline: Migrants who resisted deportation to Liberia were flown to Equatorial Guinea instead
stories.summary: Five people the US tried to deport to Liberia this week refused to leave the plane and were instead taken to Equatorial Guinea, another African country receiving migrants Washington cannot legally send home, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. Liberia had agreed to receive 20 deportees but only 15 disembarked. Human rights groups have criticised the third-country deportation deals, citing conditions and lack of legal assistance.

stories.headline: Airbus waters down its return-to-office push after strikes in Spain
stories.summary: Airbus has paused plans to cut remote working to one day a week following on-off strikes at its Spanish facilities since July and protests in France, people familiar with the matter said. Chief executive Guillaume Faury has argued for more on-site presence to improve skill-sharing and decision-making, but the company will now move more gradually after employee feedback.

stories.headline: Lula holds a four-point lead over Flavio Bolsonaro in a Datafolha run-off poll
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva would take 47 per cent against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro’s 43 per cent in a simulated second-round run-off, a Datafolha poll published on Aug 21 found, with a two-point margin of error. In July the gap was 48 to 43. In a first-round scenario Lula leads on 39 per cent to Bolsonaro’s 33 per cent. Brazil votes in October.

stories.headline: France warns of 300,000 potentially unsafe condoms
stories.summary: French anti-fraud and health agencies issued a warning on Aug 21 over tens of thousands of potentially unsafe condoms sold online, in shops and in pharmacies. About 260,000 were recalled after laboratory tests found two products risked bursting or had perforations, and a further 40,000 sold online lacked EU conformity marking or French labelling. No harm has been reported so far.

stories.headline: Japanese father reprimanded after leaving his 7-year-old alone on Mount Fuji
stories.summary: A seven-year-old boy was found sitting alone on a bench above 2,000m on Mount Fuji in fog and rain with only a soft drink and a snack, local media reported. His 48-year-old father had reportedly told him to “wait here” when he said he was tired, and continued climbing with an older son. Mountain hut staff found the child near the sixth station and alerted police, who tracked the father down at the eighth station, about a three-hour hike away, and reprimanded him.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: SimplyGo has fixed the configuration error that quietly stripped the 50-cent pre-peak discount from about 210,000 journeys a day on Aug 20 and 21, and affected commuters will be refunded. The bigger money story is housing: monthly service fees for HDB's assisted-living community care apartments will fall by 18 to 75 per cent from 2027 and the buying age drops to 55, after rising charges dulled demand. Safety ran through the rest of the day, with four fatal HDB fires in 19 days putting the difficulty of evacuating frail seniors under scrutiny. The courts were busy too, including fresh charges against the woman who ran the facility where her nephew abused primary school pupils. The buzz is confessional this week, led by a livestreamer walking back a vulgar on-air tirade — and all eyes turn to Ang Mo Kio on Sunday for PM Wong's National Day Rally.

stories.headline: SimplyGo fixes the pre-peak discount error that hit 210,000 journeys a day
stories.summary: SimplyGo says a configuration error stopped the 50-cent pre-peak travel discount from being applied to SimplyGo EZ-Link and bank card transactions on Aug 20 and 21, affecting about 210,000 journeys a day. The issue has been fixed and affected commuters will be refunded.

stories.headline: Community care apartment service fees to fall 18% to 75% from 2027
stories.summary: Monthly basic service package fees for HDB’s assisted-living community care apartments will be cut by 18 to 75 per cent from 2027 and the buying age will drop from 65 to 55, after rising charges dampened demand for newer projects. Five projects have been launched so far, in Bukit Batok, Queenstown, Bedok, Geylang and Sengkang.

stories.headline: Marriage and parenthood expected to lead PM Wong’s National Day Rally on Aug 23
stories.summary: Analysts expect marriage, parenthood and Singapore’s evolving social contract to headline Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s National Day Rally on Aug 23. Road and lane closures are planned around the venue in Ang Mo Kio.

stories.headline: LTA proposes shifting responsibility for deregistered cars to authorised exporters
stories.summary: Under a proposed Authorised Exporter Scheme, owners who hand deregistered cars to authorised persons would no longer carry disposal obligations, and rebate payouts would come faster. LTA says 122 cases of deregistered vehicles being driven illegally were recorded in the first five months of 2026, nearly double the 2024 total. Public feedback closes on Aug 28, with a transition period of at least a year for the industry.

stories.headline: DBS and POSB digital payments restored after a late-night disruption
stories.summary: DBS said at about 11.20pm on Aug 21 that customers using FAST, PayNow and SGQR on digibank and PayLah may be affected, and posted an update just before midnight saying services had returned to normal as at 11.34pm. Downdetector first showed a spike in reports at about 10.15pm. The bank apologised and said customers’ “monies and deposits remain safe”.

stories.headline: Four fatal HDB fires in 19 days expose the difficulty of evacuating frail seniors
stories.summary: Four fatal fires in HDB estates between Jul 28 and Aug 16 killed residents aged 65 to 88, prompting social agencies and MPs to call for clearer evacuation plans, better emergency alerts and fire safety education aimed at vulnerable seniors. Families describe relying on neighbours to get elderly relatives out.

stories.headline: Woman motorcyclist, 45, dies after a two-bike accident on the BKE
stories.summary: Police were alerted at about 11.30am on Aug 21 to an accident involving two motorcycles on the BKE towards the PIE. A 45-year-old female motorcyclist was taken unconscious to hospital and later died; a 32-year-old male motorcyclist was taken conscious to hospital. Motorcyclists and pillion riders accounted for 53 per cent of road deaths in 2025 despite motorcycles making up about 15 per cent of the vehicle population.

stories.headline: Two Traffic Police officers hospitalised after their patrol car caught fire on the BKE
stories.summary: The two officers were patrolling at about 12.10am on Aug 21 on the BKE towards Woodlands, at the slip road into the SLE, when they saw smoke from the engine compartment and evacuated. They and a member of the public tried to douse the fire before SCDF put it out with a water jet. Both were taken conscious to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation.

stories.headline: Tree falls on two cars in Dempsey; spa staff free the trapped driver
stories.summary: A private-hire driver was turning out of Loewen Road at about 10am on Aug 22 when a tree toppled onto his MPV, crushing the roof on the passenger side and trapping him; staff from a nearby spa freed him. A parked BMW was also hit. No one was injured, the road reopened by 5pm, and the Singapore Land Authority is investigating the cause and checking surrounding trees.

stories.headline: Car fire in a Toa Payoh carpark draws a crowd, many of them children
stories.summary: SCDF was alerted at around 6pm on Aug 21 to a fire involving the engine compartment of a car at an open-air carpark at Block 148 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, and put it out with a water jet. No injuries were reported and the cause is under investigation. Video posted on TikTok showed onlookers, many of them children in school uniform, standing close to the burning vehicle.

stories.headline: Aunt of a convicted child abuser charged with failing to protect children in her care
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman who ran a private educational facility faces two charges under the Children and Young Persons Act, according to the court’s case management system on Aug 22. She cannot be named because it could identify victims protected by a gag order. Her nephew, a 31-year-old Singaporean, was sentenced on Aug 21 to nine years and 10 months’ jail and eight strokes of the cane for abusing primary school pupils.

stories.headline: Coroner’s inquiry finds man, 21, died of a drug overdose after a pact with his girlfriend
stories.summary: A coroner’s inquiry heard that a 21-year-old man found dead at a Novena mall carpark entrance on Jun 24, 2025 had taken drugs and etomidate vaporiser pods with his then 16-year-old girlfriend, and that the pair had planned to end their lives together. A mall security guard found him and alerted police; he was pronounced dead at the scene. (If you or someone you know needs help, the Samaritans of Singapore can be reached at 1767.)

stories.headline: Woman, 28, jailed four days for a false police report against her bus driver boyfriend
stories.summary: Tang Pei Si pleaded guilty on Aug 21 to one charge of filing a false report and was sentenced to four days’ jail. She had told police in October 2024 that her 60-year-old boyfriend, a bus driver, had stolen money from her and assaulted her, after becoming upset that he could not spend time with her while working; he was forced to stop the bus, disrupting passengers.

stories.headline: Two Singaporeans among 197 arrested in a Batam illegal casino raid
stories.summary: Indonesian police arrested 197 people, including two Singaporeans, in an Aug 15 raid on an illegal casino at a lounge and bar in Batam, seizing the equivalent of S$520,731 from safes. Deputy head of the Indonesian National Police criminal investigation unit Inspector General Nunung Syaifuddin said the raid followed two to three months of investigation. Those convicted of gambling offences there face up to 15 years’ jail.
stories.source: Mothership (Batam Today, Shin Min Daily News)

stories.headline: Crocodile ‘sighting’ at Pandan Reservoir was fake; PUB files a police report
stories.summary: PUB said the photo behind a reported crocodile sighting at Pandan Reservoir was found to be fake and that it has lodged a police report. Water activities at the reservoir had been suspended a day earlier after PUB was alerted to the reported sighting.

stories.headline: 81 arrested in a four-day islandwide drug operation
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau arrested 81 suspected drug offenders in a four-day islandwide operation and seized drugs worth more than S$105,000. Weapons including katanas and knuckledusters were found in a Punggol flat.

stories.headline: CNA analysis shows how scammers spliced real footage of PM Wong into a fake Zoom call
stories.summary: A full recording shared exclusively with CNA by the Singapore Police Force shows how a fake Zoom conference was assembled almost entirely from real but obscure YouTube videos of nine high-profile figures — among them Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Minister Indranee Rajah — mixed with doctored audio and graphic overlays. The victim transferred at least S$4.9 million to the scammers, a loss the police disclosed in May; CNA’s analysis, published on Aug 22, sets out previously unreported techniques.

stories.headline: Singapore dentists split over new competency rules for wisdom tooth surgery
stories.summary: The Singapore Dental Council has introduced a competency framework under which general dentists would obtain certificates of competency for wisdom tooth surgery. The Singapore Dental Association argues this could put an artificial ceiling on career growth and that volume-based accreditation risks encouraging unnecessary surgery, while other dental leaders say it will build confidence and cut referrals to specialists.

stories.headline: AVS brings its pet adoption drive to the CBD for the first time
stories.summary: The Animal and Veterinary Service will hold Paws In The City, its first pet event in the Central Business District, at Guoco Tower Urban Park in Tanjong Pagar from Aug 27 to 29, 11am to 8pm. More than 10 animal groups will take part, with dogs, cats, small mammals and parrots up for adoption, alongside talks and workshops.

stories.headline: Skilled trades push back on the ‘unglam, dirty’ image as the local workforce shrinks
stories.summary: Tradespeople and training providers are trying to change perceptions of skilled trades to attract young Singaporeans, as the pool of local workers in these jobs continues to shrink.

stories.headline: P1 priority for parent volunteers, 28 years on: still relevant, or still unfair?
stories.summary: The Straits Times examines the Primary 1 registration priority given to parent volunteers, 28 years after it was introduced, and the continuing debate over whether it widens or narrows access to popular schools.

stories.headline: ITE student, 18, helps save a grandfather and grandson from a Buangkok flat fire
stories.summary: An 18-year-old ITE student is being credited with helping rescue an elderly man and his grandson from a fire in a Buangkok HDB flat.
stories.source: Mothership (Shin Min Daily News), The Straits Times

stories.headline: Livestreamer admits she went too far after a vulgar on-air tirade
stories.summary: Singaporean livestreamer Winnie Heng posted a video on Aug 21 acknowledging that her words were wrong and that she should have handled her emotions better, after she and fellow streamer Vadalene Eng hurled vulgarities at customers who cancelled orders for sought-after crystals following a livestream. Clips of the rant circulated on social media, and an earlier apology video was widely read as sarcastic.

stories.headline: Woman left with deep bruising after a ‘wooden board’ treatment; wellness centre apologises
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman told Shin Min Daily News she went to a wellness centre near Block 254A Serangoon Central on Aug 13 for a S$99 moxibustion promotion and was then given a “scraping” treatment in which staff tapped her legs with a wooden board, leaving dark purple bruising that had not faded days later. The centre has apologised and offered her a free treatment.

stories.headline: Keisuke Honda targets a Singapore Premier League title with FC Jurong
stories.summary: Former Japan international Keisuke Honda says “being a player is my passion” as he sets his sights on a Singapore Premier League title with FC Jurong, adding that his long-term goal remains to become head coach of the Japan national team.

stories.headline: Michelin-starred Nouri turns dinner into a play, with the chef acting
stories.summary: Restaurant Nouri and Checkpoint Theatre have created what is probably Singapore’s first true fusion of fine dining and theatre: a 10-course, three-hour experience pairing each course with a chapter from chef Ivan Brehm’s personal story, with Brehm himself performing.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Ukraine is the only theatre where people are dying in numbers this weekend, and the killing now runs both ways: 16 dead in the Kryvyi Rih mall strike, and at least six civilians reported killed inside Russia by Ukrainian drones overnight. The Iran front has gone quiet in a different way — no fighting, no talks, just a countdown to Monday, when Washington unveils sanctions it says will be the toughest ever while Tehran keeps the Strait of Hormuz all but closed. The first crack there is small but real: Iran has let a number of Iraqi tankers through after months of pressure from Baghdad. Israel's confrontations have moved almost entirely into courtrooms and capitals, from Turkey's Interpol bid against Netanyahu to a three-country condemnation over the killing of aid workers in Gaza. Two things land on Monday — the sanctions announcement, and a Franco-British-German meeting on Ukraine.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Both sides are hitting cities and economic infrastructure rather than moving the front line. The toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre settled at 16 dead and 130 injured, with four people still missing and 52 — including 14 children — in hospital; Zelensky called it 'cynical and despicable' and Russia's military has not commented. Overnight, Russian regional officials said Ukrainian drones killed at least six civilians, halting work at an Ozon logistics centre in the Samara region, where Ukraine's military says it struck the Novokuibyshevsk refinery, and killing two children at the Azov port of Yeysk. Diplomacy is stirring without a track: the French, British and German leaders co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday, while German prosecutors examine possible Russian links to a weapons cache found in woodland near Berlin.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
At least 13 people are killed in a Ukrainian drone strike deep inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The claim has not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia is using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine. Moscow and Pyongyang have not confirmed the claim.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drones strike deep into Russia overnight, killing at least six civilians, Russian regional officials say. Samara Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev reports an industrial facility hit; Ukraine's military says it struck the Novokuibyshevsk refinery. Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, says work at its Chapayevsk logistics centre has halted. Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev says two children were killed at the Azov port town of Yeysk. The Russian accounts have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian regional officials, Ukraine's military)

timeline.event: The Kryvyi Rih death toll settles at 16 dead and 130 injured with four people still missing, Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha says; 52 injured, including 14 children, remain in hospital and a day of mourning is observed across the region. The 9,000 sq m fire has been extinguished and the search may run two more days. Russia's military has not commented.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Neither fighting nor negotiating, with the next move on the calendar rather than the battlefield. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveils the sanctions package at a Monday afternoon press conference having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history', while Iran's foreign ministry calls the coming secondary measures an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations'. President Masoud Pezeshkian has said it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity'. Tehran's leverage remains the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic is a fraction of pre-war levels — though Iran has now waved a number of Iraqi oil tankers through after repeated requests from Baghdad. China, which buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil, has urged diplomacy and rebuffed US requests to help isolate Iran's economy, and NATO is facilitating escort planning among interested allies while insisting this is not an alliance mission.

timeline.event: Iran says a deal with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages.
Houthis reportedly kill six people in their first deadly attack since the start of the Iran war.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesperson stresses it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain have been assembling a coalition of about a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage, which would ultimately need Iranian acquiescence.

President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, delivered as Washington prepares to publish its sanctions package on Aug 24.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the imminent US sanctions package an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations' with 'no foundation in international law'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the measures at a press conference at 2pm EDT on Monday and is pressing Beijing to cooperate; China, which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil on 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy instead. The two sides are neither exchanging fire nor holding talks.

Ship-tracking data shows only four commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 20, none of them large crude or LNG carriers, with thousands of seafarers stranded on hundreds of vessels. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the US military helped move a seven-day average of 8 million barrels a day through the strait, against more than 20 million a day before the war.

Iran grants permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, state news agency IRNA reports. Iraqi President Nizar Amedi says passage has been facilitated in recent days but calls the issue complicated. Traffic remains far below pre-war levels and ships continue to face attacks.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Iraqi President Nizar Amedi)

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent schedules a 2pm EDT Monday press conference to unveil the sanctions package, having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history' and urged Beijing to cooperate. China buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler, and has urged diplomacy.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Contested through courts, sanctions and settlement maps rather than battle lines. Turkey said on Aug 21 it will seek an Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over Israel's interception of a Gaza aid flotilla; Israel called it a 'pathetic attempt' at intimidation and Netanyahu called Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Britain, Canada and Australia jointly called 'shameful' Israel's refusal to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Former French and British envoys are now pressing their governments to act together on the Palestinian territories, where settler expansion continues — 30 families have moved back into Kadim, evacuated under the 2005 Disengagement Plan — and Palestinian officials say Israeli forces shot dead a teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Turkey says it will seek an Interpol notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's interception of a Gaza aid flotilla, accusing him of genocide. Netanyahu responds by calling President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Neither characterisation has been tested in court.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo is about to start vaccinating against Ebola with a shot never proven against the Bundibugyo strain, which WHO's Ebola coordinator says is now spreading faster and wider than the response — half the deaths have come in the last 20 days. Europe's problems are milder but widening: West Nile virus is turning up in far more regions than at this point last season, and a Swedish festival cluster has carried measles across the water into Finland. None of this changes travel advice yet; the Ebola curve is the thing to watch, and the national daily tallies are already running well ahead of WHO's last formally ratified count.

outbreaks.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Growing exponentially in the north-east; case fatality ratio 47.5% and vaccination trial about to begin
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases and deaths in DR Congo only, as reported by DRC on 20 Aug with data to 19 Aug and carried in ECDC's week 34 threats report; 56 of 151 health zones across six provinces are affected and 1,152 people have recovered. 'Countries' counts all three with cases since May — DR Congo, Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; outbreak declared over on 28 Jul) and one imported case in France. WHO's most recent formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, data to 12 Aug) put the ratified total at 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths across those countries, so the national daily tally runs ahead of the WHO-confirmed count.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus (2026 season)
outbreaks.status: Season expanding; 21 regions reporting their first-ever cases
outbreaks.scope_note: ECDC reports locally acquired human infections in 12 countries across 99 regions so far this season, against 67 regions in nine countries at the same point in 2025. Italy and Greece carry the largest case counts; ECDC's weekly report tracks affected areas rather than a single EU/EEA case total, and does not publish a season death toll in this product.

outbreaks.name: Sweden & Finland — measles cluster linked to a music festival
outbreaks.status: All cases traced to one festival; further secondary cases likely among the unvaccinated
outbreaks.scope_note: Epidemiologically linked confirmed cases across nine regions in Sweden and one in Åland, Finland, all tied to a festival held in the Västernorrland Region from 30 Jul to 1 Aug that drew about 10,000 people. Most cases are unvaccinated children and adolescents. No deaths have been reported. Figures from ECDC's week 34 Communicable Disease Threats Report.

outbreaks.name: Europe — Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 multi-country cluster
outbreaks.status: Ongoing and rising since May 2026; eggs and chicken products the suspected sources
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases reported between May 2025 and August 2026 across the UK (207), the Netherlands (106), Belgium (15), Germany (6), France (4), Austria (2) and Denmark (1); 152 of them since May 2026. At least 34 people have been hospitalised and cases range from 0 to 90 years old. ECDC does not publish a death count for this cluster. Figures from ECDC's week 34 Communicable Disease Threats Report.

stories.headline: Ebola vaccine trial to start in DR Congo as WHO warns infections are ‘growing exponentially’
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is preparing to roll out the Ervebo vaccine, with 20,000 of an initial 70,000 doses used in a trial to test whether it works against the Bundibugyo species now circulating; the other 50,000 go to front-line health workers. There is no proven vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo. WHO’s Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis told reporters the outbreak is “growing faster and wider than the Ebola response”, that the affected area is now larger than France, and that half of all deaths occurred in the last 20 days. A Save the Children report says at least 180 Congolese children have lost both parents or caregivers since the outbreak began.

stories.headline: ECDC: West Nile virus now reported in 12 European countries this season
stories.summary: Twelve countries have reported locally acquired West Nile virus infections so far in 2026, across 99 regions, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control said on Aug 21. Italy and Greece have the most cases, at 311 and 157 respectively, and 21 regions reported their first-ever cases. For comparison, 67 regions in nine countries had reported cases by the same point in August 2025. ECDC’s Celine Gossner said the expansion shows “why Europe needs to strengthen its mosquito-control capacity”. There is no vaccine; care is supportive.

stories.headline: Measles cluster from a Swedish music festival reaches 27 cases and crosses into Finland
stories.summary: As of Aug 21, 27 epidemiologically linked measles cases have been identified across nine regions in Sweden and one in Finland, all traced to a music festival held in the Västernorrland Region from Jul 30 to Aug 1, ECDC’s week 34 threats report says. The festival drew about 10,000 people, roughly a tenth from outside Sweden. Most cases are unvaccinated children and adolescents. Finnish authorities reported a case in Åland who travelled on two ferries after exposure. ECDC rates the chance of further secondary cases among unvaccinated contacts as high, but transmission risk to the highly vaccinated general population as low.

stories.headline: Multi-country Salmonella Enteritidis cluster reaches 341 cases, with eggs the suspected source
stories.summary: A cluster of Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 across seven European countries has produced 341 confirmed cases between May 2025 and August 2026, ECDC reported on Aug 21. The United Kingdom (207) and the Netherlands (106) account for almost all of them, with smaller numbers in Belgium, Germany, France, Austria and Denmark. At least 34 people have been hospitalised, and cases range in age from 0 to 90. UK investigations point to imported eggs; Dutch work in 2026 points to chicken meat, though based on few patient interviews. ECDC expects more cases until controls reach the source.

stories.headline: WHO’s latest Disease Outbreak News puts the Bundibugyo total at 4,686 confirmed cases
stories.summary: In Disease Outbreak News 615, published on Aug 14 with data to Aug 12, WHO recorded 4,686 cumulative confirmed cases — 4,665 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 20 in Uganda and one in France — and 2,186 deaths, with at least 986 people recovered. WHO notes that with more confirmed cases than the 3,317 of the 2018–2020 outbreak, this is now the largest Ebola outbreak documented in the country. The daily national tallies reported since are higher; this remains the most recent formally ratified WHO count.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Two maximum-severity patches are the weekend's real work: Microsoft's CVSS 10.0 Entra ID flaw is already being exploited in attacks, and Cisco shipped fixes for nine Crosswork and Secure Workload bugs, five of them also rated 10.0. Exploitation is running ahead of patching elsewhere too — GitLab's critical flaw came under attack within days of disclosure, and CISA added three more bugs to its known-exploited catalogue this week. The other theme is the software supply chain, where poisoned Rust crates with a 245-million-download reach and 14 trojanised npm packages both execute at build time, so build hosts deserve the same scrutiny as production. Below that sits a steady drip of research-stage attacks on shared infrastructure, from a Cloudflare Workers side channel to a CDN amplification technique. If you patch one thing today make it Entra ID; if you audit one thing, make it your dependency lockfiles.

stories.headline: 14 trojanised npm packages drop a RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor with AI-assisted command and control
stories.summary: Researchers found 14 trojanised npm packages that install a RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor, whose operators use AI assistance in their command-and-control workflow. Development teams should audit recent npm installs and lockfiles on Linux build hosts.

stories.headline: New SynkLoader malware pushed through Microsoft Teams help-desk phishing
stories.summary: Expel researcher Marcus Hutchins identified a previously unknown loader, SynkLoader, delivered by attackers impersonating IT help-desk staff over Microsoft Teams and pointing victims to a fake “PowerShell Cleaner” MSI hosted on Azure. It ships a fake Windows 11 lock screen to capture passwords, plus system profiling, remote access and persistence; researchers note Alt+Tab exposes the ruse. Its focus on mapping Active Directory suggests it is a precursor to ransomware. No victim count or named actor has been disclosed.

stories.headline: Microsoft Defender’s own boot-time driver can be turned against security software
stories.summary: Check Point Research describes a technique that abuses a Microsoft Defender driver executing early in boot to delete security software files before those products start, giving an attacker with the right access a way to disable endpoint defences.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Check Point Research

stories.headline: Android car malware spreads through built-in vehicle updaters for ad fraud and proxy botnets
stories.summary: Malware is reaching Android-based in-car infotainment systems through their built-in update mechanisms, enrolling vehicles in ad-fraud and residential-proxy botnets.

stories.headline: Hundreds of leaked AWS keys found giving full control over corporate accounts
stories.summary: Researchers found hundreds of exposed AWS access keys, a large share of them with permissions broad enough to take full control of the corporate accounts behind them. Rotate long-lived keys and scan repositories and build artefacts for credentials.

stories.headline: CISA orders federal agencies to patch two actively exploited TrueConf Server flaws
stories.summary: CISA added two TrueConf Server vulnerabilities — a code injection flaw and a missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-72529) — to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 20 and set a federal remediation deadline.
