Any internet-facing TrueConf deployment should be patched now.

stories.headline: Microsoft patches a maximum-severity Entra ID flaw exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Microsoft has patched a CVSS 10.0 Entra ID vulnerability allowing remote code execution, which it says has been exploited in attacks, alongside a privilege-escalation fix. Tenants should confirm the update has applied and review sign-in and privileged-role logs.

stories.headline: Cisco patches nine Crosswork and Secure Workload flaws, five scoring CVSS 10.0
stories.summary: Cisco has released fixes for nine vulnerabilities across Crosswork and Secure Workload, five of them rated the maximum CVSS 10.0. These are management-plane products with deep network reach, so patch on the vendor’s timeline rather than the next maintenance window.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Cisco advisory, NVD

stories.headline: Hackers abuse FTP server banners to deliver new Windows malware
stories.summary: A campaign hides payload staging instructions in FTP server banner text, a channel most monitoring ignores, to deliver a new Windows malware family.

stories.headline: SickKids data breach exposes employee and job applicant information
stories.summary: Toronto’s Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) disclosed a breach exposing employee and job applicant data. Patient care systems were not reported as affected.

stories.headline: GitLab flaw comes under active exploitation days after disclosure
stories.summary: Attackers began exploiting a critical GitLab vulnerability within days of its disclosure. Self-managed GitLab instances, especially internet-facing ones, should be upgraded immediately and checked for signs of unauthorised access to repositories and CI runners.

stories.headline: Rust supply chain attack plants build-time malware in crates with 245 million downloads
stories.summary: Attackers poisoned the widely used arrayref crate and others to run infostealer malware at build time, reaching a dependency tree with roughly 245 million cumulative downloads. Rust teams should pin and audit dependencies and treat build machines as compromised if affected versions were pulled.

stories.headline: Suspected Russian hackers abuse Google OAuth and WhatsApp device linking to hijack accounts
stories.summary: A campaign attributed by researchers to suspected Russian operators abuses legitimate Google OAuth consent flows and WhatsApp’s linked-device feature to take over accounts without stealing passwords. Review linked devices and third-party app grants.

stories.headline: AI-generated exploit scripts target Siemens S7 PLCs in US critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Researchers report exploit scripts, apparently generated with AI assistance, aimed at Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers in US critical infrastructure. Operators should verify PLC network segmentation and remove any direct internet exposure.

stories.headline: Cryptographic context injection attack could let web pages steal Grok chat data
stories.summary: A newly described cryptographic context injection technique could allow a malicious web page to extract a user’s Grok chat data. It is research-stage rather than observed in the wild, but is the same class of cross-context leak that keeps surfacing in browser-embedded AI assistants.

stories.headline: isolated-vm flaw lets sandboxed JavaScript escape to the host
stories.summary: A flaw in the isolated-vm Node.js library allows code running inside the sandbox to reach the host process, opening a path to remote code execution for services that use it to run untrusted JavaScript.

stories.headline: Critical Elementor Pro bug lets unauthenticated attackers upload PHP and run code
stories.summary: A critical flaw in the Elementor Pro WordPress page builder allows unauthenticated file upload leading to remote code execution. Sites should update to the patched release immediately; Elementor is one of the most widely installed WordPress plugins.

stories.headline: Critical NetScaler flaw bypasses authentication on Gateway and AAA servers
stories.summary: Citrix is urging administrators to patch as soon as possible after disclosing a critical NetScaler vulnerability that can bypass authentication on appliances configured as Gateway or AAA virtual servers — the same class of edge device repeatedly targeted in past NetScaler campaigns.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a Zimbra SNMP flaw for unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.summary: An OS command injection flaw in Zimbra Collaboration Suite is being exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 21.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: ‘Zombie Card’ attack can revive expired Visa cards for contactless payments
stories.summary: Researchers describe a technique that can bring expired Visa cards back into use for contactless payments, bypassing expiry checks in parts of the transaction flow.

stories.headline: CDN Tsunami attack abuses HTTP/3 translation for up to 350x DoS amplification
stories.summary: A technique dubbed CDN Tsunami abuses how content delivery networks translate HTTP/3 requests to achieve amplification of up to 350 times, turning CDN infrastructure into a denial-of-service multiplier.

stories.headline: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
stories.summary: Vulnerabilities in NASA’s open-source AIT-GUI ground software could allow unauthenticated attackers to issue spacecraft commands. The toolkit is used beyond NASA, so any operator running it should restrict network access and apply fixes.

stories.headline: CISA warns of hackers exploiting a critical MLflow vulnerability
stories.summary: CISA added a server-side request forgery flaw in the MLflow machine-learning platform to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 19 after observing exploitation. MLflow servers are frequently exposed inside ML platforms with broad internal network reach.

stories.headline: Manic Android malware exfiltrates data from offline phones via nearby infected devices
stories.summary: ThreatFabric describes Manic, active since at least February 2026, which combines spyware, banking fraud and remote control, targeting at least 169 banking, government eID, payment, crypto wallet, messaging and authenticator apps. Its stand-out feature is peer-to-peer exfiltration over Wi-Fi Direct and Bluetooth, relaying stolen data through nearby infected devices when the command-and-control server is unreachable. Ukraine is the primary focus, with victims also in Central and Western Europe, the UK and Russia.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Workers Spectre attack leaks a JWT from a co-located worker
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated a Spectre-style side-channel on Cloudflare Workers that leaked a JSON Web Token from a co-located worker at about 12 bits per second — slow, but a reminder that multi-tenant edge runtimes still carry speculative-execution risk.
